newsitem.title: MALI: Mali revives independence day celebrations.
newsitem.headline: Mali revives independence day celebrations.

text.p: Mali revived its independence day celebrations for the first time in eight years on Sunday with a large military and civilian parade in the capital.

President Alpha Oumar Konare presided over the march-past with tens of thousands of Malians looking on. Members of the armed forces, paramilitary units and civilian groups such as scouts and traditional hunters took part.

Konare and his civilian government, who face presidential and parliamentary elections next year, revived formal independence celebrations in response to popular demand expressed during a state radio phone-in last year.

In previous years, the government urged Malians to mark the anniversary of their 1960 independence from France with a day of "meditation and reflection" in the light of economic problems faced by the country.

Mali has won praise from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund for its economic reforms but ordinary Malians say they have yet to see the benefit. Trade unions have demanded a 50 percent hike in public sector pay.
Konare, a historian elected in 1992 during Mali's democratic transition, urged the nation on Saturday to prepare for next year's elections to ensure they were free and fair.
"Whatever the programmes and the convictions, the people are the final arbiter," he said in a broadcast address to the nation.
